one_sentence_story: In 1920, John Watson and Rosalie Rayner showed that seven pairings of an unexpected steel-bar clang with a tame white rat taught 11-month-old 'Little Albert' to fear furry cues — a famous demonstration of emotional conditioning clouded by fading effects, textbook myths, and never reversing the child's fear.
so_what_for_you: When an everyday place, sound, or animal triggers an outsized gut flinch from one bad past pairing, remember Mary Cover Jones's 1924 antidote: calm, gradual, safe re-exposure teaches the alarm system that the cue no longer predicts danger.
